conditions.overall: Wild streams have been fishing well after recent rain, with a brief sweet spot as water cleared but hadn't fully dropped. Water levels have since fallen but fish are still active and feeding.

tactics: The best fishing on wild streams came after the water cleared up but hadn't fallen out completely — capitalize on that sweet spot after rain events.
As water levels drop, stay back from the hole you're fishing as much as possible to avoid spooking fish.
Use smaller dry flies and nymphs to avoid causing too much commotion on the surface — this will pay dividends in low water.
Dry dropper fishing is the recommended approach for the wild creeks.
Delayed Harvest season ends June 6 — once catch-and-keep opens on NC delayed harvest streams, fishing drops off quickly; seek other stream options for a better shot at catching fish.
For wade fishermen on the Watauga and South Holston tailwaters, follow the TVA generation schedule closely when targeting fish on foot.

waters.name: Wild Streams (Western North Carolina)
waters.note: Fishing well after recent rain. Best action came while water was clearing but still slightly elevated. Fish are still happy and eating well even as levels have dropped further.

waters.name: NC Delayed Harvest Streams
waters.note: Delayed Harvest season ends June 6, 2026. Once catch-and-keep opens, fishing drops off quickly. DSO recommends seeking other stream options. Next stocking will occur in October and November.

waters.name: Watauga River (Tailwater, East Tennessee)
waters.note: After months of low water, all-day generation is now occurring. Fishing great on high water for drift boat anglers. Wade fishermen should follow the generation schedule.

waters.name: South Holston River (Tailwater, East Tennessee)
waters.note: All-day generation now occurring after months of low flows. Reports haven't been as good as the Watauga, but folks are still catching fish. Wade fishermen should follow the generation schedule.

elevation_note: High Country streams (Boone, 3300-4000ft) run 1-2 weeks behind lower-elevation WNC
stocking_note: NC Delayed Harvest streams will not be stocked again until October and November, following the end of the Delayed Harvest season on June 6, 2026.
